title: Saluki: Finding Taint-style Vulnerabilities with Static Property Checking
authors: Ivan Gotovchits, Rijnard van Tonder, David Brumley
abstract: We present Saluki, a new tool for checking taintstyle (data dependence) security properties in binary code. Saluki provides a domain specific language for expressing taint-based policies. Saluki can find vulnerabilities in real programs for a number of CWE types, including those for command injection, weak PRNG seeds, and missing sanitization checks such as SQL escape routines or checks on buffer lengths. Saluki includes two new ideas in binary program analysis. First, Saluki uses flux, a new static analysis technique for path-sensitive, contextsensitive recovery of data dependence facts in binaries. Second, Saluki introduces a sound logic system for reasoning over data dependence facts. We develop a domain-specific language on top of our logic system to express security properties as formal specifications. Saluki includes a decidable solver procedure to prove (based on the underlying logic) whether a set of data dependence facts satisfy a security property. Our evaluation shows that Saluki is capable of finding vulnerabilities in COTS x86, x86-64, and ARM software, including 0-days
explain_beginner: This paper introduces a tool called Saluki that examines software even when the original source code is not available, only the compiled binary. It looks for a common kind of security flaw where unsafe data flows into a dangerous operation, such as a command or a database query. Saluki lets experts describe these unsafe flows in a simple language, then automatically checks whether a program has them. The authors tested it on real software for common processors and found previously unknown security holes. This matters because it can catch serious bugs in everyday programs before attackers do.
explain_business: This research shows that a tool can scan compiled software for dangerous data flows without needing source code, which is common with third-party or legacy systems. It found real, previously unknown vulnerabilities in commercial software across major processor types. For an executive, this means security reviews can extend to binaries you cannot inspect directly, reducing blind spots in supply chains and inherited code. The decision it informs is whether to invest in binary-level static analysis as part of due diligence, procurement, or ongoing vulnerability management, especially where source access is limited.
explain_practitioner: The authors built Saluki to check taint-style data dependence properties directly in binaries. It offers a domain-specific language for specifying taint policies. Two technical contributions stand out: flux, a static analysis that recovers path-sensitive and context-sensitive data dependence facts, and a sound logic for reasoning over those facts. A decidable solver then proves whether the recovered facts satisfy a given security property. The evaluation found vulnerabilities in commercial off-the-shelf x86, x86-64, and ARM software, including zero-days, covering command injection, weak PRNG seeds, and missing sanitization checks.
